_contract: Shared cross-language tokenizer fixture (architecture review 2026-07-29, candidate #6). Both wasm-core/src/text_tokenizer.rs (mod tests::parity) and src/utils/__tests__/TextTokenizer.parity.test.ts read this file directly and assert their own real tokenizer's output against it. This file IS the contract — not a copy of one side's behavior, the single source of truth for what each side is expected to produce, for both the cases where they agree and the cases where they're documented to diverge. See CONTEXT.md's TextTokenizer entry for the fuller narrative.

cases.name: chinese_chars_agree
cases.description: Both sides classify Chinese characters individually, one token per char.

cases.name: latin_word_agrees
cases.description: Both sides consume an entire Latin word as one token.

cases.name: number_agrees
cases.description: Both sides consume an entire run of digits as one token.

cases.name: whitespace_run_agrees
cases.description: Both sides consume a run of whitespace as one token, distinct from surrounding words.

cases.name: ascii_punctuation_agrees
cases.description: Both sides classify a single ASCII punctuation char the same way.

cases.name: decimal_point_splits_number_agrees
cases.description: Neither side's number-matching spans a decimal point — both split into number/punctuation/number.

cases.name: punctuation_run_grouping_diverges
cases.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: JS's regex catch-all groups a run of consecutive punctuation into one token. Rust's char-by-char classifier emits one token per char — dictionary lookups are single-char keyed, so per-char is safer against truncation. Deliberately unfixed.

cases.name: cjk_extension_a_diverges
cases.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: Rust's is_chinese_char covers CJK Extension A (U+3400-4DBF); JS's regex chinese group only checks U+4E00-U+9FFF (一-鿿). JS's catch-all types it punctuation instead.

cases.name: compatibility_ideographs_diverges
cases.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: Rust's is_chinese_char covers Compatibility Ideographs (U+F900-FAFF); JS's regex chinese group does not. Mirror-image of cjk_extension_a_diverges.

cases.name: underscore_diverges
cases.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: JS's \w excludes '_' from every regex capture group (chinese/latin/digit/whitespace all reject it, and the punctuation catch-all [^\w\s...] also rejects it since \w matches '_'), so it falls into the gap-fill path and is typed 'unknown'. Rust's catch-all has no \w-shaped exclusion, so '_' becomes 'punctuation'.

cases.name: bom_diverges
cases.description: KNOWN DIVERGENCE: ECMAScript's \s regex class matches ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (U+FEFF, the UTF-8 BOM) per spec. Rust's char::is_whitespace() does not (U+FEFF isn't in Unicode's White_Space property) — Rust's catch-all types it punctuation instead.
